chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Sa'd bin Abdullah, from Muhammad bin Abdul-Hameed, from 'Amer bin Riyah, from Amru bin Waleed, from Sa'd al-Iskafi, from Ja'far bin Muhammad, peace be upon them both, that he said:
Three things that are back breakers: a man who considers his deeds to be much, forgets his sins and is admired by his opinion.

key_terms.أَعْجَبَ بِرَأْيِهِ: Admired by his opinion (arrogance in one's own judgment)
key_terms.اسْتَكْثَرَ عَمَلَهُ: Considered his deeds to be much (overestimating good works)
key_terms.قَاصِمَاتُ الظَّهْرِ: Back breakers (metaphor for things that weaken or break one's spiritual standing)
key_terms.نَسِيَ ذُنُوبَهُ: Forgot his sins (neglecting self-accountability for wrongdoings)

ai.seo_question: What are the three things that break the back of a believer's faith?
ai.summary: In *Mani al-Akhbar*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), framing these three traits as 'back breakers' that collapse the structural integrity of a believer's spiritual posture. This teaching highlights the Shia emphasis on *muraqabah* (mindfulness of God) and *tawadu* (humility), warning that self-satisfaction and the neglect of one's faults lead to a fragility in faith comparable to a physical collapse. The 'breaking of the back' serves as a metaphor for the loss of dignity and strength in the hereafter due to these internal spiritual defects.
